h2: Choosing an ultrasonic testing company in Seattle: field UT, aerospace labs and in-line inspection
html:
Choosing an ultrasonic testing company in Seattle: field UT, aerospace labs and in-line inspection

"Ultrasonic testing services" is one search phrase for at least three different purchases around Seattle. Field UT on steel structures, piping, tanks and hulls is what Atlantis provides. Production UT of aerospace parts is laboratory work done to prime contractor rules. Ultrasonic in-line inspection is a pipeline service that sends a tool through the line. Knowing which one you need saves a round of quotes.

Field UT, Nadcap laboratory or in-line inspection?

  • Field ultrasonic testing means a Level II technician with a portable flaw detector or thickness gauge at your site: remaining wall on corroded plate and pipe, shear-wave examination of welds, lamination checks before cutting or welding. Atlantis does this work.
  • Aerospace production UT, such as immersion scanning of forgings, plate and composite parts for an aircraft program, is done in laboratories that hold Nadcap accreditation and the prime contractor's approval when the purchase order requires them. Atlantis is not a Nadcap-accredited supplier, so a search for Nadcap accredited NDT services should go to those laboratories.
  • Ultrasonic in-line inspection sends an instrumented tool through a pipeline to map wall loss or cracking along its length. Specialist in-line inspection vendors run those tools on the operator's behalf. Atlantis is not an ILI company; at excavations it can take UT readings to check what the tool reported, as described on pipeline inspection services.

What about tube inspection and "advanced" ultrasonic testing?

For boiler and heater tubes, conventional UT gives wall thickness from the outside at chosen points; see ultrasonic boiler tube thickness testing. Full-length inspection of exchanger tubes from the bore uses specialist rotating or electromagnetic probes that fall outside this page's conventional scope. Phased array and automated UT also sit outside the conventional scope covered here. If your code or client names a specific technique, put it in the request so every supplier quotes the same work.

Washington rules that create field UT work

Two state programs keep field UT in steady demand. The Department of Ecology expects regulated oil-handling facilities to inspect their tanks under API 653, and that inspection needs shell thickness by course at known locations. The Department of Labor and Industries issues certificates for boilers and pressure vessels, and measured wall at fixed points is what lets an owner or commissioned inspector defend an inspection interval. Both need readings that can be found again next time, which is a field job, not a laboratory one.

Who offers ultrasonic testing around Seattle

The Kent valley holds aerospace testing laboratories. Mistras, for example, describes its Kent branch as a combined field services operation and in-house laboratory that is an FAA repair station, holds Nadcap and AS9100D credentials and carries approvals from aerospace primes, with engineering services alongside. Regional field firms and refinery contractors cover industrial UT, and shipyards often keep their own gauging technicians. A field provider like Atlantis competes on a narrower job: Level II UT on site, procedures approved by a named ASNT Level III, and data that your inspector, surveyor or engineer can use directly.

Questions that separate one UT provider from another

  • Is the person on site certified Level II in UT under the employer's written practice? In industry an "ultrasound inspector" is a UT technician, so ask for the certification record, not a job title.
  • Does the written procedure name the probe type and frequency, the beam angles for weld work and the reference block, and has an ASNT Level III approved it?
  • Will thickness data arrive as a grid or CML table you can import, with the nominal and minimum values you supplied?
  • Who applies the acceptance criteria: the technician against a stated code table, or your engineer?
  • Will next year's survey use the same probe, setup and location plan, so readings can be compared?
  • When is the report due? Get the date in writing.

Seattle work Atlantis takes on

Atlantis sends UT technicians from Houston to Seattle, Tacoma and the Puget Sound refinery and terminal sites for thickness surveys and weld UT, adding MT or PT where surface cracking matters. Useful pages: ultrasonic pipe thickness testing, ultrasonic weld inspection, ultrasonic testing in Tacoma, ultrasonic testing in aviation, inspection services in Washington and ASNT Level III consulting for UT procedures. Teams building their own capability can start with UT Level 2 training. Send the scope through the Seattle UT enquiry; we reply within one business day.
